Welcome to Tower Hill Primary School
On behalf of Tower Hill Primary School I welcome you to our website. We hope it gives you a taste of what life is like at our outstanding school. Situated in the Ancient Village of Cove (mentioned in the Doomsday Book) in the Western part of Farnborough, we are a two-form entry, inclusive Primary School, that sits at the heart of a vibrant and diverse local community.
At Tower Hill Primary School our core vision is that ALL children will be equipped with the skills, knowledge, understanding and empathy that will lead to them being able to make their own choices in life, successfully. We strive for all to be actively engaged in their own learning, to be motivated and eager, to achieve and attain to their own full potential – thus making them proud of themselves and of being a member of the ‘Tower Hill Team’. Our relationships between all members of Tower Hill are held as key to our success. We value each member of the school community as an individual and interact with them honestly, respectfully and politely.
We have an ethos of ‘no ceiling to learning and achievement’ for our children irrespective of their ability, and the school’s outstanding record of achievement including both its impressive academic results and most significantly in the progress pupils make as they pass through the school, highlight the success of this approach.
Our key values of Respect, Friendliness, Achievement, High Expectations, Confidence and Fairness pervade through our curriculum and ensure that our children's spiritual, moral, social and cultural development in this ever changing world as well as their physical well-being enables them to thrive in a supportive, highly cohesive learning community.
We are very proud of our school and are very happy to welcome visitors at any time to look round, please don’t hesitate to contact us.

pageCache.pageTitle: Tower Hill Primary School - Welcome to Year 1
pageCache.text:
Children
Welcome to Year 1
Our classes are Blackpool and Spinnaker.
In Blackpool the class teacher is Miss Kirk and the Learning Support Assistant is Miss Maddie.
In Spinnaker the class teacher is Miss Fensome and the Learning Support Assistants are Mrs Durkin and Mrs Amero.
Miss Mizer will also support across both rooms.
Our PE Days are Tuesday (indoor) and Wednesday (outdoor.) Children are expected to come into school in PE kit. That is a white t-shirt, dark blue or black shorts/trousers, black jumper and trainers.
Reading books and diaries should be brought into school every day. Please aim to read with your child at least 3 times a week and record in their reading diary when they have read with you.
Homework menus will be sent out for each half term. Please bring this work into school or email a photo to the relevant class email.
We are really looking forward to working with your children. Please speak to a member of the year 1 team if you have anything to share or discuss.
Our class emails are:
blackpool@towerhil.hants.sch.uk
spinnaker@towerhill.hants.sch.uk
Miss Kirk and Miss Fensome
Blackpool Tower
Spinnaker Tower

Children
Welcome
Our classes are Canton and Petronas.
In Canton Class we have Mrs Hicks, Mrs Armsworth, Miss Nicholls and Ms Hunter.
In Petronas Class we have Mrs Wilkins and Miss Hens.
Our PE Days are Tuesday (Outdoor) and Wednesday (Indoor.) Children are expected to come into school in PE kit. That is a white t-shirt, dark blue or black shorts and trainers.
We send out spelling homework on a Tuesday. We expect the children to write out their spellings and if they can, write a sentence with their spelling in it. This needs to be returned the following Monday so the children can complete their spelling quiz at the back of their spelling homework book. This homework is very beneficial as it covers the year one and two common exception words that the children need to include in their class writing.
We are really looking forward to working with your children. We have an open door policy and love to hear all about the children's exciting news.

Welcome to Year 4
We would like to extend a very warm welcome to all our Year 4 children and families. We are looking forward to an exciting year of learning, discovery and achievement.
In Petrin Class, the class teacher is Miss Prior, supported by Miss Smith and Mr Sealey. If you need to contact Petrin Class, please email petrin@towerhill.hants.sch.uk.
In Skylon Class, the class teacher is Miss Monnery, supported by Miss Beers-Baker. If you need to contact Skylon Class, please email skylon@towerhill.hants.sch.uk.
PE lessons will take place on a Monday and Thursday, and children should come to school wearing their full PE kit on these days.
Homework will be set weekly on MyMaths, and your child’s login details can be found in their reading journal.
Reading remains a top priority, and we ask that children read at home at least three times each week, with this being recorded in their reading journal. We are excited to work together to make this a successful and enjoyable year!
Any questions, please don't hesitate to contact us.
Miss Prior and Miss Monnery

pageCache.pageTitle: Tower Hill Primary School - Modern Foreign Languages
pageCache.text:
Learning
Modern Foreign Languages
Intent: At Tower Hill Primary School our core vision is that ALL children will be equipped with the skills, knowledge, understanding and empathy that will lead to them being able to make their own choices in life, successfully. The intent of our French curriculum is to design a curriculum that helps Pupils develop communication and literacy skills that lay the foundation for future language learning.
We believe the learning of a foreign language provides a valuable educational, social and cultural experience for all pupils. They develop linguistic competence, extend their knowledge of how language works and explore differences and similarities between a foreign language and English. Learning another language raises awareness of the multilingual and multicultural world and introduces an international dimension to pupils’ learning, giving them an insight into their own culture and those of others. The learning of a foreign language provides a medium for cross-curricular links and for reinforcement of knowledge, skills and understanding developed in other subjects.
The teaching should provide an appropriate balance of spoken and written language and should enable pupils to express their ideas and thoughts in another language and to understand and respond to its speakers, both in speech and in writing.
French at Tower Hill should lay the foundations for further foreign language teaching at key stage 3, leading on to further study and ultimately, equipping pupils to study and work in other countries across a global economy. Where possible teachers will embed Tower Hill’s golden thread of aspiration within French units, whilst always underpinning the diverse application of language skills across a range of occupations.
We strive for all to be actively engaged in their own learning, to be motivated and eager, to achieve and attain to their own full potential in French and as such a variety of techniques alongside formal teaching are used to encourage the children to have an active engagement with French, including games, role play and action songs.
Implementation: Tower Hill’s French Curriculum fosters pupils’ curiosity and deepens their understanding of the world. The teaching of French enables pupils to express their ideas and thoughts in another language and to understand and respond both in speech and in writing. Language teaching should provide the foundation for learning further languages, equipping pupils to study and work in other countries. Through the implementation of our French Curriculum, learning should be consolidated and built upon each year, ensuring that the children make good progress and leave each phase of their learning with the relevant skills, knowledge and understanding.
Early Years & Key Stage I:
At Tower Hill Primary school, French is taught to children in Reception and Key Stage I through the learning of songs, rhymes, greetings and other short opportunities to practise with their class teachers. For example, registration, numeracy mental warm-ups and class routines can be used to target the use of French.
In Key Stage II, the children follow a more structured scheme of work in weekly 30 minute sessions delivered mainly by the French Leader (AHT).The curriculum provides an appropriate balance of spoken and written language and should lay the foundations for further foreign language teaching at Key Stage 3. It enables pupils to understand and communicate ideas, facts and feelings in speech and writing.
In KSII pupils will be taught to:
A variety of techniques are used to encourage the children to have an active engagement with the French, including games, role play and action songs. Puppets and soft toys are often utilised to demonstrate and present the foreign language. Flashcards or other pictorial representations, even mime, are used to present new vocabulary, as this serves to demonstrate the foreign language without the need for translation. Audio recordings, websites and videos provide an additional model of the spoken language and contact with native speakers is encouraged wherever possible to involve the children in learning about culture.
In French, we assess the impact of the curriculum on our learners in a number of ways. Children’s progress is assessed informally and continuously during the lessons by the teacher. We consider it important that progression is measured and ensured through skill levels, not by endlessly growing lists of vocabulary. Ultimately, the Impact of Tower Hill’s French curriculum will be measured in the children’s enthusiasm and enjoyment of the language. Our curriculum should foster a love of learning modern foreign languages and lay the foundations for further foreign language study at Key Stage 3.
